items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone

ctx.x: George, can you tell, who else was in the band? Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone, Lee Collins on trumpet, and with the addition of Buddy, maybe we had two trumpets for us. Yes.

And a seven-piece arch. Well, now in this story, it's slightly different from the story I've had before, because I've heard that you played with Buddy, or he played with you in George Orson's song. Then you had some kind of a, you know, Buddy didn't get on with Buddy or something, and you fired Buddy, and you got Lee Collins after Buddy left. No, I don't remember that.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Me and Lee and Son Andy, Roy Evans, Joe Robeshow, and Plekton, Rennie Hall. That's all we had.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Well, let me put another record on it.

And he never played no trumpet. All the small, you know, cornet. Great fellow you are. We had a good battle. Jesse Cesar, the helicopter. Little Roy. Who's that now? I want you to tell me without lookin' at it. Who plays trumpet like that? Who plays trumpet like that? I know it's got your boys on there. I know you recognize it. Who plays trumpet like that? Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Yes, Louie. Yes, Louie. It sounded like it. That's old Shags. Lee. That's Lee, huh? Lee Collins. What did you call him?
Shags. Shags, huh? That's Lee Collins.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: I worked in that place two years, man. Me and Lee and Sonny Andy. Roy Evans. Joe Robeshoe. And Plekton. Rennie Hall. That's all we had.

ctx.x: I mean, why he got off it, I don't know. Uh-huh. And, uh, that was a bad consist of Roy Evans, Son Handy, Lee College, myself, Joe Rovershow. And that was all. No, Plectum. We called the guy Plectum. So that'd be one of the greatest band you'll play around here. I'll do his name, and I'll see if I can think his name now. I call him Plectum, because he had one of them Plectum guitars. Five-string guitars. Banders, now. What is that little fella's name, man? He turned out to be one of the greatest, he's New York…
Yeah. Well, he had a couple of them, he had Rene Hall and he had Rene Hall. Rene Hall, that's it, that's it.
